goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_024) Compare five major optimization algorithms used in deep learning — SGD with momentum, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, and AdamW — on their adaptive behavior, convergence properties, and known failure modes. State which is preferred for training large Transformer models and why.
ground_truth: SGD+momentum: fixed global learning rate with velocity accumulation; strong generalization on well-tuned problems; fails with heterogeneous gradient scales. AdaGrad: per-parameter LR adapts inversely to accumulated squared gradients; good for sparse NLP features; failure mode: LR decays monotonically to near-zero on long runs. RMSProp: exponential moving average of squared gradients fixes AdaGrad decay; good for non-stationary objectives like RNNs; no bias correction. Adam: combines RMSProp with momentum bias correction; fast default convergence; can converge to sharp minima with worse generalization than SGD on vision tasks. AdamW: decouples weight decay from gradient adaptation (fixes the L2 regularization conflation in Adam); now the standard for Transformer pretraining because it improves regularization in large models.
